Herjeet Marway est doctorante, sa thèse porte sur « L’éthique globale ». Elle est rattachée au Département de Philosophie à l’Université de Birmingham en Grande Bretagne. Ses recherches juxtaposent les théories sur l’autonomie au pouvoir d’agir des femmes instigatrices de violence (notamment, les femmes qui se suicident en faisant exploser des bombes attachées à leurs corps). Son travail cherche à démentir les perceptions (erronées) de rôles genrés « acceptés », et souligne que les modèles libéraux d’autonomie et de pouvoir d’agir (agency) ne parviennent pas à expliquer la violence perpétrée par des femmes. Marway se tourne donc plus volontiers vers des théories relationnelles pour expliquer les choix et les actes de ces femmes. Marway s’intéresse aussi à la théorie féministe, l’éthique de la vertu, la bioéthique, et la philosophie politique. Quelques publications récentes : « Scandalous Subwomen and Sublime Superwomen : Exploring Portrayals of Female Suicide Bombers Agency », Journal of Global Ethics, 2011, vol. 7, n? 3

Jane F Apperley qualified in medicine from the University of Birmingham (UK) in 1979 and she completed specialist training in hematology in Birmingham, London and Cambridge (UK). During this time she spent 2 years as a post-doctoral fellow at the Children's Hospital in Boston (MA, USA). She was appointed as Senior Lecturer and Honorary Consultant Physician to the Hammersmith Hospital in 1993, and was later promoted to Reader (2000) and then Professor of Haemato-oncology (2002). She is now Chief of Service for Clinical Haematology at the Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust and Chair of the Department of Haematology at Imperial College. Her particular interests are the biology and management of CML, which has led naturally to an extensive experience in stem cell transplantation. She is past President of both the European Group for Blood and Marrow Transplantation and the British Society of Blood and Marrow Transplantation, and serves on the advisory board of the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research

Michael Grimble was born in Grimsby, England. He acquired a BSc (Coventry), MSc, PhD and DSc degrees from the University of Birmingham. The Institute of Measurement and Control awarded him the 1991 Honeywell International Medal . He was awarded an IEEE Fellowship in 1992 and he was recognised at the 1993 Edinburgh International Science Festival as one of Scotland's four most cited Scientists. He was appointed a Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh in 1999
